events.title: Orestes drives Western Emperor Julius Nepos from Ravenna
events.description: The general Orestes seized Ravenna and Julius Nepos fled to Dalmatia. Orestes then made his young son Romulus Augustulus emperor; he would be the last to rule in the West.
events.html: The general Orestes seized Ravenna and Julius Nepos fled to Dalmatia. Orestes then made his young son Romulus Augustulus emperor; he would be the last to rule in the West.

events.title: Tang and Silla forces destroy the Yamato fleet at Baekgang
events.description: Near the mouth of the Geum river in south-western Korea, Tang and Silla forces fought the fleet of Yamato Japan, sent to support the Baekje restoration movement. The Tang navy destroyed the Japanese fleet, ending hopes of reviving Baekje.

events.title: Guy of Lusignan begins the siege of Acre
events.description: Guy of Lusignan, King of Jerusalem, began the siege of Acre, his first significant counterattack against Saladin and part of what became the Third Crusade. The siege lasted until July 1191 and ended in a key crusader victory.

events.title: The Treaty of Birgham is ratified at Northampton
events.description: The second Treaty of Birgham, under which Margaret, Maid of Norway, was to marry Edward of Caernarfon, son of Edward I of England, was ratified at Northampton. Scotland was to remain separate from England, but Margaret died on her voyage to Scotland.

events.title: Pedro Menéndez sights Florida and names it for St Augustine
events.description: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés sighted the Florida coast on the feast of St Augustine and gave the saint's name to the harbour. He founded the settlement on 8 September; it is the oldest continuously occupied European city in the US.
events.html: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés sighted the Florida coast on the feast of St Augustine and gave the saint's name to the harbour. He founded the settlement on 8 September; it is the oldest continuously occupied European city in the US.

events.title: First issue of Scientific American is published
events.description: Inventor Rufus Porter launched Scientific American as a weekly in New York. It is the oldest continuously published monthly magazine in the United States.
events.html: Inventor Rufus Porter launched Scientific American as a weekly in New York. It is the oldest continuously published monthly magazine in the United States.

events.title: Martin Luther King gives his 'I Have a Dream' speech
events.description: Speaking to some 250,000 people at the March on Washington, King described his dream of a nation free from racial injustice. The march helped build support for the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
events.html: Speaking to some 250,000 people at the March on Washington, King described his dream of a nation free from racial injustice. The march helped build support for the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

events.title: New Orleans orders its first mandatory evacuation as Katrina nears
events.description: With Hurricane Katrina at Category 5 in the Gulf of Mexico, Mayor Ray Nagin ordered the city's first-ever mandatory evacuation. Tens of thousands without transport sheltered in the Superdome.
events.html: With Hurricane Katrina at Category 5 in the Gulf of Mexico, Mayor Ray Nagin ordered the city's first-ever mandatory evacuation. Tens of thousands without transport sheltered in the Superdome.
